title: Infeasible, unbounded, or the solver can't tell

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A water utility's pump-scheduling MIP gets INFEASIBLE_OR_UNBOUNDED from HiGHS with default settings. Rerun with presolve switched off, HiGHS says UNBOUNDED. What should the team conclude?

options.text: The first answer stands, since switching presolve off can hide an infeasible model
options.says: On the lesson's models every infeasible one stayed INFEASIBLE with presolve off; nothing was hidden.

options.text: The model is unbounded, since presolve had left HiGHS unable to tell the two apart
options.says: Right: presolve's objective-based steps caused the hedge; without them HiGHS answers definitely, so look for a missing bound or term.

options.text: The model is infeasible, since presolve off makes HiGHS call such MIPs unbounded
options.says: The infeasible MIP in the lesson's table stayed INFEASIBLE with presolve off.

options.text: Neither answer counts, since only Gurobi can separate the two cases
options.says: A zero-objective copy separates them on any solver, and HiGHS with presolve off did too.

origin.section: Five Solvers Give Three Answers for the Same Unbounded Model

questions.stem: A fleet model comes back INFEASIBLE_OR_UNBOUNDED. You clear its objective and solve the copy, which comes back OPTIMAL with every vehicle idle. What is the original model?

options.text: Infeasible, since a plan with every vehicle idle earns nothing at all
options.says: An idle plan is still a plan: the copy has the same rows and bounds, so the original has plans.

options.text: Optimal, since the copy found an optimal plan for the same rows
options.says: Every plan is optimal for a zero objective; it says nothing about the original objective.

options.text: Unknown, since the copy answers a different question than the original
options.says: The copy answers exactly the open half: whether any plan exists.

options.text: Unbounded, since the original has plans and the solver still hedged
options.says: Right: a plan exists, so the hedge can only have meant unbounded.

questions.stem: A nightly run on a 2,000-project portfolio stops at its 60-second limit with NO_SOLUTION_FOUND and primal status UNDETERMINED. What should the service tell the planners?

options.text: No plan was found in the 60 seconds, and plans may still exist
options.says: Right: a limit with no plan claims nothing about the model; rerun with more time.

options.text: No plan exists, as the 60 seconds showed, so run the conflict finder
options.says: Only INFEASIBLE proves that no plan exists; this run proved nothing.

options.text: The model is unbounded, as the 60-second stop shows, so add a bound
options.says: UNBOUNDED is a separate reason; a time limit says nothing about rays.

options.text: The empty plan is best, as nothing was found within the 60 seconds
options.says: No plan at all was found, the empty one included; the run ended before any.

origin.section: A Limit Without a Plan Means "Unknown", Never "Infeasible"

concepts: what a stopped search with no plan claims
